title: Adding with apples
examples: Teacher, if I have two apples and you give me one more, how many do I have?
What does it mean to put apples together when we count?

explain.say: Today we are going to learn about putting numbers together.
If you have three apples and I give you one more apple, we put them together.
We can find out how many altogether by counting every single apple.
Let us count four apples and then add two more apples to them.
In real life, we put things together when we count our toys.
A common mistake is to only count the biggest group of apples.

faq.q: What does 'putting together' mean when we count?
faq.a: It means joining two or more groups of things into one big group. You count everything in that one group.
asks: What does it mean to add apples?
How do I count things together?

faq.q: If I have two apples and three more, how many altogether?
faq.a: You count them all: one, two, three, four, five. You have five apples altogether.

faq.q: Do I count the first group or the second group?
faq.a: You must count all the apples from both groups. We count them all to find the total.
asks: Do I just count the first pile?

faq.q: Can I use fingers to help me count?
faq.a: Yes, using your fingers is a great way to help you count things that are small. You can count on your fingers.
asks: Can I use my hands to count?

faq.q: What if the apples are not all the same size?
faq.a: It does not matter if they are different sizes. We count them by how many there are, not how big they look.

facts: We use counting to find the total amount.
The total is how many altogether.

quiz.say: If you have two apples and add one more, how many altogether?
quiz.why: You count the two apples, and then you count the one more apple to get three.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you counted the two apples twice.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you only counted the last apple.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you forgot to count the extra apple.

quiz.say: Three apples and two apples put together make how many?
quiz.why: You count the three apples, and then you count the two apples to get five.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only counted the second group.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you counted all the apples too many times.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only counted the first group.

quiz.say: If we put four apples and one apple together, what is the total count?
quiz.why: When you put four and one together, you count them all to reach five.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you counted the apples more than they are.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you only counted the last apple.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you left out counting the extra apple.
